endorsements.quote: Therefore, AI should aim to augment clinician capabilities rather than replace human expertise and responsibility in medical decision-making.
Robust technical safeguards encompassing encryption, access controls, and cybersecurity measures are fundamental to preventing data breaches and ensuring patient confidentiality.

Mitigating such potential harm will require the aspects of diversity and inclusion to be integral throughout the AI development lifecycle, from design choices in data sampling and labeling to testing systems on representative populations.
Therefore, strong data governance policies, transparency protocols, personnel training, and ethical values embedded across teams are essential in the handling of health data by AI systems.

unlisted_practices: Conduct ongoing audits of AI system performance after deployment and recalibrate as needed.
Incorporate digital health and AI training into medical education curricula.
Involve patients and communities in AI deployment decisions through open dialogue about the technology's values and risks.
Use collaborative forums and policy sandboxes to strengthen AI oversight and evolve governance structures.
Prioritize physicians' professional judgment over algorithmic outputs when they conflict.
